doc: One concrete correction per square, written after looking at the picture, for squares whose redraws kept reproducing the same fault: build_rework_jobs.py puts it in the job under 「具体怎么改」, after (not instead of) the reviewer's own note. Delete an entry once the square passes. See handoff/opus-74-decisions-2026-11-03.md.

notes.1-john-1-1: Jesus and every disciple must have clearly cropped hair: the nape bare, the hair ending above the robe collar, no hair block beside the jaw, never shoulder-length. Not shaved, not buzz-cut, no faded or shaved sides. Draw each man's cut slightly differently.
notes.1-samuel-20-1: The boy who runs for the arrows must wear a plain tunic that falls below his knees - no shorts, no bare thighs. Keep him running, keep the bow, the arrows and Jonathan where they are.
notes.2-kings-10-1: The two spear-bearing guards at the palace gate must not wear a Roman or Greek cuirass or a strap skirt (pteruges). Dress them as 9th-century-BC Israelite guards: a knee-length tunic under a plain bronze scale corselet, a simple round or conical bronze helmet, no cape, no muscle breastplate.
notes.2-kings-24-1: Remove the many-arched stone bridge over the water at the left. Leave the river open, with a shallow ford or a low timber pier causeway on wooden posts instead. No rounded masonry arches anywhere in the picture.
notes.2-samuel-19-1: The soldier in the Roman segmented cuirass with the strap skirt and short sword must be redrawn as a 10th-century-BC Israelite soldier: knee-length tunic, plain bronze scale corselet, spear or long straight sword. No banded plate, no strap skirt, no gladius.
notes.ephesians-4-1: The workers on the upper-right scaffold must wear working tunics that fall below the knee; no bare thighs. Everything else in the scene stays as it is.
notes.exodus-13-17: Remove the paddle-shaped prickly-pear and the spiny columnar succulents at the bottom of the scene. Use Sinai desert plants instead: acacia, tamarisk, white broom (rotem) and dry tussock grass. No cactus pads, no spines, no agave rosettes.
notes.ezekiel-36-22: Remove the multi-span round-arched stone bridge in the middle distance. Leave a plain riverbank with a shallow ford. No masonry arches anywhere.
notes.ezekiel-37-1: The man in red in the foreground and the kneeling man in white must wear tunics that fall below the knee; no bare thighs on any of the revived men. Keep the bones, the valley and the prophet.
notes.ezekiel-38-1: Remove every branching columnar cactus from both rocky slopes and from beside the fortress; use cypress, terebinth and dry thorn scrub instead. The fleeing men on the right must wear tunics that fall below the knee, with hems down, not raised.
notes.isaiah-26-1: Remove the multi-arch stone bridge near the centre-right. Put a shallow ford with stepping stones there instead. No masonry arches anywhere in this Old Testament scene.
notes.isaiah-36-1: Remove the tall pitched-roof tower with the cross-shaped finial above the city in the upper right. In its place draw a plain square Judean fortress tower: flat roof, simple crenellations, no spire, no pitched roof, no finial and no cross anywhere in the picture.
notes.jeremiah-10-1: The hammering worker at the left and the green- and blue-clad workers must wear working tunics that fall below the knee; no bare thighs. Keep the idol workshop exactly as it is.
notes.joshua-5-13: Keep the commander as a man with his sword drawn - Joshua 5:13 says a man stood over against him - but dress him for the Late Bronze Age: a long belted tunic and a plain bronze scale corselet, no Roman muscle cuirass, no red cape, no Roman soldiers' tunics behind him. Also remove the agave/cactus-like plants at the lower right and use thorn scrub and terebinth.
notes.obadiah-1-17: Remove the Greek columned temple with the triangular pediment at the upper right and the multi-arched stone bridge over the river; draw Iron-Age Judean flat-roofed stone buildings and a shallow ford instead. The celebrating people on the right steps must wear tunics that fall below the knee.
notes.psalms-115-1: The two men breaking the idol at the lower left must wear working tunics that fall below the knee; no bare thighs. Keep the broken idol and the worshippers.
notes.psalms-31-1: Remove the three large wooden crosses mounted on the room wall: this is David's chamber, centuries before the cross, and nothing Christian belongs in the room. Draw plain plaster, a lamp niche and a hanging rug there instead. The spear-bearing guards across the ravine must wear tunics that fall below the knee. Do not change the small emblem in the top-left corner.
notes.psalms-82-1: Replace the colonnaded buildings with triangular pediments on the background terraces (upper right and far left) with Judean and Ancient Near Eastern architecture: flat-roofed stone halls, terraced vineyards and cedar groves. Keep the central pillar of light exactly as it is - God is light here, never a human figure.
notes.psalms-91-1: Remove the red-and-white-robed teacher figure entirely: this is an Old Testament psalm and God must never be drawn in human form, and no figure of Jesus belongs in it. Draw the shelter of the Most High as light pouring into a rock shelter with the shadow of great wings over it, and the psalmist's household beneath - a crowd, as the fact card asks, not five or six people - looking up to the light. No haloed man, no human face in the sky, no New Testament figure.
notes.psalms-94-1: No three similar figures anywhere. Give the men on the upper steps clearly different ages, hair colour, beard shape and robe colour, and place them at different heights and distances, never symmetrically as three. Do the same for the two maroon-robed men at the left so each face and head of hair is plainly a different person. Keep the rays of light, with no figure in them.
notes.revelation-9-1: The fleeing bearded man at the far left and the green-clad child in front of him must wear garments that fall below the knee; no bare thighs. His hair must end above his collar, not on his shoulders.
notes.zechariah-8-1: Remove the Greek colonnaded temple complex on the hill at the upper right. Draw post-exilic Judean hill terraces instead: flat-roofed stone houses, olive groves and vineyard walls. No columns with triangular pediments anywhere.
